The 24 port holes come out of expand.py that way; the USB's is the same aperture turned through the placement's own 90 degrees."},"dip-bank":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED as geometry, UNNAMED as a thing. A strip of ten small switch cells with red caps at both ends sits at x 30.4-49.4, y 32.6-36.0 mm, below the RST button. Callout 8 of cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 has its leader drawn to this strip and its own list names item 8 'Reset button' - which the quick-start contradicts, drawing and labelling RST as the round button above (fig-0008). Both cannot be right. The round button is modelled as the reset; the strip is drawn as panel decor and registered as a gap rather than given a function neither document states. Its printed label is two words at roughly 1 mm cap height and does not resolve at 3.2 px/mm."},"figure-choice":{"note":"Gate 1. cor580-qsg/fig-0007 panel 0, box [6,37,808,116], is orthographic to 0.19 percent (1.8294 px/mm on x, 1.8329 on y) and is the reference for every VERTICAL number here. cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 0, box [8,111,1410,251], is 1.55 percent out - its box too tall by the render's own shadow - but at 3.198 px/mm on x it is twice the quick-start's resolution, so it is the source of every HORIZONTAL number. Its y readings were mapped into the orthographic frame by the two-point fit y' = 1.0128 y - 0.045, anchored on the two port-row centres the two figures share (17.55/31.56 there against 17.73/31.92 here); every vertical number taken off the datasheet below is quoted after that map. THE PREPARED BRIEF'S BAND REPORT WAS NOT USED: it profiles cor580-qsg/fig-0004, which is the Edge-core wordmark, not a chassis."},"info-tab":{"note":"photo - the green pull-out tab at the bottom right of the front face reads 414.4-432.5 x 39.9-42.7 mm in cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 and is drawn again in cor580-qsg/fig-0014. The sibling has the same tab within 2 mm of the same place; this one was measured anyway, and agrees. Neither document names it, so it is drawn as common/pull-tab@1 and its function is not claimed."},"legends":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED - the two paired legends are centred as STRINGS, not on their arrows. 'MGMT (up)(down) CONSOLE 1' spans 388.2-404.7 mm, whose centre 396.45 is the jacks' own centre to 0.05 mm, but its arrow pair therefore sits at 394.7 - 1.8 mm left of the parts it joins - because CONSOLE 1 is five glyphs longer than MGMT. 'OOBF 0 (up)(down) OOBF 1' has equal halves and its arrows land at 376.35 against the cages' 377.0, which is centred to a third of a millimetre and is drawn on the cages. The MGMT/CONSOLE 1 string needed a decision and got it twice. The vendor prints its arrows at 394.70 against the jacks' centre of 396.34 - not a miss but a consequence, because CONSOLE 1 is five glyphs longer than MGMT and the vendor centres the STRING, whose own span of 388.2-404.7 centres on 396.45, which is those jacks to a tenth of a millimetre. Drawn at the measured 394.70 it is 1.64 mm off and L61 fires; drawn shifted bodily right at cap height 1.5 the arrows centre but CONSOLE 1's last glyph runs into the USB trident at 407.0, which the vendor's own spacing clears. What resolves both is the cap height. It reads 1.25-1.67 mm across the four strings in this cluster and 1.5 was the first guess; 1.4 is equally inside that spread, and at 1.4 the string can shift the 1.64 mm that puts its arrows on the jacks and still stop at 406.30, clear of the trident. So: cap height 1.4 throughout the cluster, MGMT ending at 393.64, arrows at 396.34, CONSOLE 1 starting at 398.74. The legend is drawn 1.64 mm right of where the vendor prints it and the numbers above are the record of that; nothing on this face is now nearly-but-not centred."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched and found nothing. One web search, 'Edgecore COR580 AS9926-24D end of life end of sale announcement' (2026-08-29), returned Edgecore's 2020 Q4, 2021 May and 2022 July EOL notices - none of which names this model - alongside a live product page and datasheet revision R04. `eol: none-announced` means the vendor has announced nothing, not that nobody looked."},"management-cluster":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED, and it is NOT the sibling's cluster - different parts, different order, one of them rotated. Read off cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 at 3.198 px/mm and corroborated in cor580-qsg/fig-0014, which labels every item. Left to right: a micro-USB console ('CONSOLE 0') at 350.2-359.6 x 19.6-22.4; two stacked SFP+ out-of-band cages ('OOBF 0' upper, 'OOBF 1' lower) at 369.0-385.0, tops at 12.0 and 27.5, pitch 15.5; the 1000BASE-T management RJ-45 above the RS-232 console RJ-45 ('MGMT' / 'CONSOLE 1'), both centred on x 396.34 - the mgmt jack's two bezel LED windows read at 391.34 and 401.34 and its bezel rails at 389.46 and 403.22, which fix that centre twice over - and a USB-A. Both RJ-45s carry WHITE bezels here where the sibling's are dark - on common/rj45-port@4 that meant the default skin and not its `dark` one; that part is gone with the RJ45 sweep, and its white/dark skins went with it. MGMT is now common/rj45-eth@1 and CONSOLE 1 is std/rj45@2, and both draw the same dark housing, so the white-versus-dark distinction the photo shows is no longer drawn. The sibling's cluster shares a single shell between its mgmt RJ-45 and its USB, puts the SFP+ pair on the RIGHT and has no micro-USB at all. Nothing here was carried over."},"method":{"note":"THIS DEVICE WAS MODELLED FROM ITS SIBLING, library/devices/edgecore/dcs510 (AS9716-32D), which shares this chassis shell exactly - 438.4 x 536 x 43.1 mm, two rear PSU bays, six rear fan trays, the same 1RU Accton frame. Every number below is marked CARRIED OVER (taken from the sibling and, where said so, corroborated against COR580's own figures) or MEASURED (read here, off the figures named). The distinction is the point: an inherited number and a measured one are different kinds of fact. Nothing on the FRONT face was carried over except the idiom - this faceplate is not the sibling's."},"oob-leds":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED - one lamp per out-of-band SFP+ port, printed as `(lamp) (up)(down) (lamp)` ABOVE the upper cage at y 9.5 mm. The row profiles at x 373.05 and 379.61 for the lamps with the two arrow glyphs between them at 375.14 and 377.33; the group's own centre, 376.3, sits within 0.7 mm of the cages' 377.0, so it is drawn on the cage centre and the lamps at +/-3.28. The up/down pair is the same convention the port numerals use, so the left lamp belongs to the upper cage. Semantics from the quick-start: 'SFP+ 10G OOBF LEDs: Green (10G), Amber (1G)'."},"panel-decor":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED - the vent fields. A tall field at the left end (x 1.0-28.0, y 2.2-39.7), a block right of the seven-segment window (59.6-74.2 x 11.2-22.6), a band above and a band below the port field (78.0-346.0, y 1.6-10.0 and 38.2-41.8), two blocks flanking the micro-USB (346.0-367.0), and a field at the right end beyond the USB (414.6-436.6), all read off cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 and cor580-qsg/fig-0007. The DIP strip is drawn as decor for the reason given above."},"port-count":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED, and it is NOT the sibling's. 'Switch Ports: 24 x 400 GbE QSFP-DD' (cor580-datasheet/doc.md:76) and '24 x 400G QSFP-DD ports' in the quick-start overview. Drawn as TWELVE columns of two, not the sibling's sixteen: the twelve cage columns are countable in cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 and each column carries one numeral pair."},"port-led-cutouts":{"note":"NOT punched, deliberately, and for the sibling's reason. common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1 declares FOUR openings, so expand.py refuses to derive one hole for it - deriving from the body would punch a 1.8 x 11.4 slot and claim the metal has a slot where cor580-qsg/fig-0013 plainly draws four windows, at a resolution (3.2 px/mm on the datasheet elevation) that cannot measure any one of them. L39 stands on all 24 lamps and standing is the correct outcome until somebody reads the metal on a real unit."},"port-led-offset":{"note":"each lamp column is CENTRED on its port - dy = (10.0 - 11.4) / 2 = -0.70 on both rows - and, exactly as on the sibling, that is a decision taken AGAINST the measurement. Mapped into the orthographic frame the top row's lamp block centres at 17.03 against its ports' 17.73 and the bottom row's at 32.91 against 31.92, so the two lamp columns sit 15.88 mm apart belly to belly against the port rows' 14.19. THAT IS THE SIBLING'S FINDING REPRODUCED: it measured 16.03 against 14.1-14.4 on a different figure of a different product, and chose to centre because the reading rests on peak-finding at 1.8-3.2 px/mm and on cages whose lit top lip reads their height short. Two devices now show the same ~1.7 mm spread, which is the strongest argument yet that it is real rather than noise - and it is still not a caliper. Centred here for consistency with the sibling, and this note is the record for whoever overturns both at once."},"port-leds":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED, and the sibling's PART fits. Four lamps per port on a 3.03 mm vertical pitch in a column beside the cage, the columns BRACKETING each 2-wide shell exactly as on the sibling. The two sub-columns in the gutter between shells 4 and 5 read at x 167.29 and 169.17 mm (1.56 mm wide each, cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 at 3.198 px/mm), which puts the left column's body 2.91 mm left of its cage and the right column's 20.35 mm right of its cage - hence the per-column offset list. Lamp centres in one column read 12.31, 15.39, 18.47, 21.40 mm on the top row and 28.01, 31.09, 34.17, 37.09 on the bottom. common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1 is 1.8 x 11.4 on a 3.0 mm pitch, which is this to 0.03 mm, so the sibling's component is used unchanged. The quick-start's '400G: 1 LED Blue' names what LIGHTS in 400G mode, not how many lamps the metal has: fig-0013 draws four."},"port-numbering":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED, and it is NOT the sibling's. This faceplate numbers from ZERO. The printing is `n (up)(down) n+1` on one baseline under each column - '0 (up)(down) 1' under column 1, read at 5x in cor580-datasheet/fig-0007, and '20 (up)(down) 21', '22 (up)(down) 23' read directly in cor580-qsg/fig-0013 - so ports run 0..23, even on the TOP row and odd on the bottom, column-major. `index-origin: 0` on the group and `number-from: 0` on the block. Carrying the sibling's 1-origin would have mislabelled all 24."},"port-numeral-baseline":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED - the numeral glyphs read y 24.58-25.70 mm in cor580-datasheet/fig-0007, which puts the baseline at 25.70 and the arrow pair's centre at 25.10. The numerals sit 3.1 mm either side of their column centre: '20' reads at 309.57 and '21' at 315.82 against column 10's measured centre of 313.63."},"port-positions":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED. Column centres read off the dark cage runs in cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 0 at 3.198 px/mm: 92.40, 111.63, 136.65, 156.04, 181.05, 200.28, 225.45, 244.53, 269.54, 288.77, 313.63, 332.08 mm. The five group pitches (first column of one 2-wide shell to the next) are 44.25, 44.40, 44.40, 44.09, 44.09 - mean 44.25 - and the six within-shell steps average 19.23. The within-shell pitch modelled is the REGISTRY's 19.0 (spec/schemas/standards.yaml qsfp-dd states no pitch key, so w IS the pitch and instances abut), not the 19.23 measured; the gutter was then solved so the LAST column lands where it was measured - 11x19.0 + 5*gutter = 239.68 gives gutter 6.14 - which keeps the far end of the face exact. Worst residual is 0.6 mm at column 8. Row centres 17.73 and 31.92 mm are the dark cage runs in cor580-qsg/fig-0007 (1.8329 px/mm, panel box [6,37,808,116]); row-pitch 14.19. The sibling's block (at [38.23, 12.13], gutter 6.06, row-pitch 14.37) was not reusable and none of it was reused."},"power":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED against the sources, and THE TWO DISAGREE. The datasheet states both numbers and distinguishes them - 'Max PSU power: 1300 W' and 'Max power usage: 800 W' (cor580-datasheet/doc.md:109-110). The quick-start's Switch Chassis block says 'Power Consumption: 1300 Watts maximum', which is the PSU rating restated in the consumption row. 800 W is the chassis DRAW and is what power-max-w records; 1300 W is the supply rating and lives on common/psu-ac-1300@1. The vendor states no typical and no ambient, so the envelope is unstated. THE SIBLING RECORDS 1300 AS ITS DRAW: carrying that over would have overstated this box by 500 W."},"psu-parts":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - the FRU table names FSH082-610G as the AC PSU and FSJ033-610G as the DC 48 V PSU (cor580-datasheet/doc.md:196-197), and AS9926-24D/24DB-FAN as the single fan tray SKU. Different part numbers from the sibling's, which is why they are recorded here rather than inherited."},"rear-ground-points":{"note":"CARRIED OVER, corroborated. The quick-start's FRU list item 7 says '2 x grounding screws' and both are visible at the bottom corners of cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 1; the left one reads 3.1-12.5 mm in x. It is drawn at 1.0, as on the sibling, so that it does not overlap the PSU bay."},"rear-layout":{"note":"PART CARRIED, PART MEASURED, AND THE CARRIED FAN GEOMETRY WAS WRONG. The sibling's rear is PSU, six fans, PSU with PSU bays at 9.0 and 372.4 (57 wide), fan bays 46.6 wide on a 48.8 pitch from 73.9, and grounding points at the bottom corners. That whole arrangement was taken over, and this entry said 'corroborated to better than a millimetre' until the fan bay was measured properly, at which point it was not. . MEASURED HERE, on cor580-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 1 at 3.198 px/mm and again on an 8x crop of it at 25.7 px/mm: tray 6's OPENING runs 75.2 to 116.1 mm, the chassis pillar carrying the '6' runs 116.4 to 124.4, and tray 5's opening starts at 124.8. The fan bay is therefore 40.9 mm wide at 75.2 + n x 48.79, NOT 46.6 wide at 73.9 + n x 48.8 - 5.7 mm too wide and 2.0 mm too far left if inherited. The tell that sent me back to it is arithmetic, not eyesight: the sibling's geometry leaves a 2.2 mm divider between trays, and the vendor prints a 3.4 mm numeral on that divider. 3.4 does not fit in 2.2. The real divider is 8.3 mm and the '6' is centred in it, reading 120.1 against the divider's own centre of 120.45. So this device gets its own tray contract, common/fan-module-41@1, measured here; common/fan-module-46@1 is not used. THE SAME ARITHMETIC IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE SIBLING, which shares this shell and prints the same numerals on the same dividers, and whose own contract records reading a 46.7 mm frame with a 2.2 mm gap. One of the two readings is of the tray FRAME and the other of the OPENING, and they cannot both be the bay. Not resolved here because DCS510's figures were not opened for this run. . CORROBORATED, not merely carried: the six red fan handles start at 75.98, 124.77, 173.55, 222.95, 271.73 and 320.51 mm, a pitch of 48.79, 48.78, 49.40, 48.78, 48.78, mean 48.79 against the carried 48.8, and they sit 0.7-1.4 mm inside the openings above. The handle block's centre, 218.42, is the chassis centre to 0.8 mm. The PSU faces bound at 65.4 on the left and 371.3-373.0 on the right, against the carried 66.0 / 372.4. . STILL CARRIED AND NOT MEASURED, listed so it is not mistaken for the above: the PSU bay WIDTH of 57.0 and its left edge of 9.0 - COR580's own release latch reads from 6.57, so the bay is drawn 2.4 mm right of the module's own edge, the same trade the sibling records to keep the bay off the grounding lug; every VERTICAL rear number (bay y 1.5, bay height 40.0, lug y 26.0), because this panel is the non-orthographic one at 2.93 percent and is the worst surface on the device for a y; and the PS1 legend's x of 369.0, which is the mirror of the PS2 legend measured here at 69.1 rather than my own weaker reading of 365.4 off the right-hand crop. Fans are numbered 6 to 1 LEFT TO RIGHT, printed on the divider to the right of each tray. PS2 is the left supply and PS1 the right."},"rear-psu-arrows":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED, and the sibling's mark is WRONG for this device. Each PSU legend carries an arrow above it, and they are MIRRORED: PS2's points LEFT and PS1's points RIGHT, each toward the supply it names (verified at 14x on cor580-datasheet/fig-0007, x 210-250 and 1160-1200 px). The sibling draws both as one left-pointing path and calls it an airflow arrow. Carried over unchanged, PS1's arrow would have pointed away from its own supply. Drawn here with `mark: arrow-left` and `mark: arrow-right`, and no claim is made about what they mean - this box has only front-to-back SKUs, so an airflow arrow that reverses between two identical supplies is not an airflow arrow."},"seven-segment":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED - a two-digit seven-segment readout at x 40.7-58.1, y 11.3-23.4 mm, right of the system LEDs.
